narrative:
The model predicts you have a 13% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a high probability, it is enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the norm, but in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees the complete lack of past setbacks as a warning sign rather than a strength. 

The second most important influence is your strong desire to pursue higher education. This works in your favor and pulls the prediction toward passing, which makes sense because every student who passed also expressed this ambition.

Third, your reason for choosing this school—wanting to be close to home—also nudges the outcome slightly toward failing. Most students who succeeded chose the school for its course offerings or reputation rather than location.

Taken together, the absence of any prior academic struggle combined with your home-focused school choice slightly outweighs the positive signal from your higher-education goals, leading the model to flag a risk of failure.

To improve, you should focus on building consistent study habits beyond your current low weekly study time, make fuller use of the family support you already receive, and consider extra academic activities. Strengthening these areas now can turn the 13% risk into a clear pass. (248 words)
